projects.name: User Discovery Plan & Survey
projects.description:
Class assignment for the whole team: one submission, 10 points, uploaded as a file.
### Part 1: User observation and interview plan
- Our target user population
- How we'll do user discovery (qualitative and quantitative methods)
- Who we'd interview or observe, with numbers. The prompt's example: administrators at 6 public schools, or 15 households served by a client NGO.
### Part 2: The instrument
- An interview guide, survey, focus group guide or workshop agenda that our partner could use.
- Other groups give feedback in week 6. The class also suggests sharing it with our partner for input.
- Guides and examples are in the resources module on [bCourses Modules](https://bcourses.berkeley.edu/courses/1556923/modules). An example household survey from the Pickering Lab is linked on the assignment page.
Our drafts: the User Discovery Plan and the Google Form.

projects.name: Conduct user discovery
projects.description:
Class assignment for the whole team: one submission, 5 points, graded complete or incomplete. Text entry or file upload.
- Carry out the plan from the Oct 2 assignment, or have our partner carry it out.
- In the bCourses text box, record how many interviews we did or what data we collected. No report needed.
- If interviews or workshops aren't feasible with our target users, talk to the teaching team about adapting the assignment.
- Be ready to present what we learned, and what got in the way, in our team project update.
### In class we'll discuss
- What did we learn through user discovery?
- How could the survey or interview guide be better?
- What do we still not know about users' preferences and practices?
- What insights could shape our solution design?
- If discovery isn't done, what is in the way?
Heads-up: this is due one week after the survey is submitted, so responses need to start coming in right after Oct 2.

projects.name: Farmer guide
projects.description: Two-page guide on pre-harvest irrigation water quality and post-harvest washing. Drafts go to our client on Nov 6; he shares the guide with farmers on Nov 13.

projects.name: Business or distribution model
projects.description:
Class assignment for the whole team: one submission, 10 points. Text entry or file upload.
Outline a business or distribution model for our solution: a set of hypotheses about how it gets produced, distributed, sold or financed, and maintained. It builds on our Theory of Change and starts us thinking about how to evaluate impact. Try several alternative models before picking the strongest.
### Turn in
1. The Social Business Model Canvas, with all 14 boxes filled in.
2. A one-page write-up with the details, including unintended consequences and how we'd prevent or reduce them.
### The 14 boxes
Key stakeholders, social mission, social value proposition, social impact measurement strategy, key channels, key relationships, key delivery partnerships, key activities, key resources, competitors and coopetition, macro-environment (PESTEL), revenue streams, cost structure, and surplus.
### Unintended consequences to think about
- Competitors or existing sellers we'd displace
- Environmental harm
- Other negative spillovers
The Mural template and a PNG download of the canvas are linked on the bCourses page. We can make several versions of the canvas, one per alternative model.
Heads-up: the farmer guide drafts go to our client the same day at 5 PM.
